title: A short proof of the modified Kretschmann-Schlingemann-Werner conjecture
abstract: Let $Φ_1, Φ_2 : \mathbb{M}_d(\mathbb{C})\to \mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ be two quantum channels with respective Stinespring isometries $V_1, V_2 : \mathbb{C}^{d}\to \mathbb{C}^{n} \otimes \mathbb{C}^{m}$ on any common dilation space $\mathbb{C}^{m}$. We prove that there exists a unitary $U$ on $\mathbb{C}^{m}$ such that $\|V_1-({\bf1}\otimes U)V_2\|_\infty\leq\sqrt{2\|Φ_1-Φ_2\|_\diamond},$ thus resolving vom Ende's modification of the Kretschmann-Schlingemann-Werner conjecture in the affirmative.
summary: This paper resolves a modified version of the Kretschmann-Schlingemann-Werner conjecture concerning quantum channels. It proves an inequality bounding the operator norm difference between two Stinespring isometries by the diamond norm distance between their corresponding quantum channels. This result provides a powerful quantitative tool for comparing quantum processes.
main_problem: The paper addresses a modified version of the Kretschmann-Schlingemann-Werner (KSW) conjecture, which relates the distance between two quantum channels to the distance between their Stinespring representations.
main_result: It proves that for any two quantum channels $\Phi_1$ and $\Phi_2$, there exists a unitary $U$ such that the operator norm distance between their respective isometries satisfies $\|V_1-({ f1}\otimes U)V_2\|_\infty\leq\sqrt{2}\|\Phi_1-\Phi_2\|_{\diamond}$.
method: The proof utilizes advanced tools from quantum information theory, including the diamond norm ($\|\cdot\|_{\diamond}$), operator norms ($\|\cdot\|_{\infty}$), and properties derived from the Stinespring dilation theorem.
model_or_system: The system under study involves general quantum channels $\Phi: \mathbb{M}_d(\mathbb{C})	o \mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$, which are completely positive and trace-preserving maps. These channels are analyzed via their Stinespring isometries $V$.
key_observables: Diamond norm distance ($\|\cdot\|_{\diamond}$) between channels, and the minimum operator norm distance $\min_{U\in U(m)} \|V_1 - (1 \otimes U)V_2\|_{\infty}$ between the Stinespring isometries.
important_parameters: The constant factor $\sqrt{2}$ in the derived inequality is shown to be optimal.
main_assumptions: The proof holds for any common dilation space $\mathbb{C}^m$ associated with the channels.
paper_structure: The paper establishes relationships between various norms and uses mathematical tools like Lemma 3 to derive the final inequality, resolving the modified KSW conjecture in the affirmative.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous quantitative link between the operational distance (diamond norm) of quantum processes and the structural distance (operator norm) of their underlying representations, which is fundamental for characterizing process fidelity in open quantum systems theory.
